definition: A technique that stores and reuses the processed representation of frequently repeated prompt content (such as a long system prompt) to avoid redundant computation on subsequent requests.
details: Prompt caching can significantly reduce latency and cost for applications that repeatedly send the same or overlapping context, such as a fixed system prompt or a large document referenced across many queries.

explainer.lead: Prompt caching stores and reuses the processed representation of repeated prompt content so later requests skip redundant computation. It matters because applications resending a fixed system prompt or long shared document save latency and cost.

tiers.eli5: It is like keeping a chopped-up ingredient ready in the fridge instead of re-chopping it every time you cook the same dish.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers place stable content such as a long system prompt at the front of requests so it can be cached and reused across queries. A pitfall is that caching only helps when content genuinely repeats or overlaps.
tiers.paperLevel: The processed representation of frequently repeated prompt content is stored and reused, avoiding recomputation on subsequent requests; the benefit depends on repetition of the content.

explainer.example: An app sends the same long system prompt with every user query; with caching, the processed form is reused instead of recomputed each time.
